name: dispatch-pilot
description: Dispatch Pilot: a decision model outside Claude (Jev or Clef, your choice) picks the main agent's reasoning effort each time you send a message, sets it on every request of the turn, and decides it again every few steps while the turn runs. It also picks the model and effort of each agent the main agent dispatches and of each agent a Workflow script starts. The main agent's model never changes, so the prompt cache survives (on a Claude Code subscription; not on Bedrock, Vertex or a gateway, where switching effort breaks the cache). It also keeps the full skill listing out of the main agent's context and suggests the few skills that fit each message; mid-turn, the main agent can look skills up with the find_skill tool. When an agent's tool calls keep failing it raises that agent's effort (a failing haiku agent goes on as sonnet), unless the failures are what the work expects.

decisionModel.title: Decision model
decisionModel.description: Which model makes the decisions: jev (TypeSafe; needs the TypeSafe API key) or clef (Cloudflare Workers AI; needs the Cloudflare account ID and API token). The other is never used as a fallback: when the chosen one fails, the message goes on unrouted. Some options default by the model chosen. With Jev they are set to what Jev accepts (up to 32 recent messages and 16 steps within a 6000-token context budget). With Clef, which answers more slowly and sometimes reads only the start of a long request, the decision timeout is 3000 ms, the context budget at most 2000 tokens (4 messages, 4 steps), and skill suggestions start off (/dp skills on turns them on).

typesafeApiKey.title: TypeSafe API key
typesafeApiKey.description: Key for TypeSafe's System One API, where Jev runs (used when the decision model is jev). Without one, nothing is sent and every turn keeps the session's effort.

cloudflareAccountId.title: Cloudflare account ID
cloudflareAccountId.description: The Cloudflare account that runs Workers AI (used when the decision model is clef). It is part of the request address, which Claude Code's debug log records. Without it, nothing is sent and every turn keeps the session's effort.

cloudflareApiToken.title: Cloudflare Workers AI API token
cloudflareApiToken.description: A Cloudflare API token that can run Workers AI (used when the decision model is clef): in the dashboard, Workers AI, Use REST API, Create a Workers AI API Token. Without one, nothing is sent and every turn keeps the session's effort.

timeoutMs.title: Decision timeout (ms)
timeoutMs.description: How long a message waits for the decision model (200 to 8000). Past it the message goes on unrouted, at the session's effort, and the status line says so. Default: 1500 with Jev, 3000 with Clef, which answers more slowly (a first request often takes 1.5 s or more).

contextMessages.title: Recent messages sent
contextMessages.description: How many recent messages the decision model reads beside yours (0 to 32): their text and the names of the tools they called, never file contents or tool output, secrets masked. Default 32 with Jev (the context budget, not this count, ends what is sent), 4 with Clef.

contextTokens.title: Context budget (tokens)
contextTokens.description: How many tokens your message and the recent messages may take together (100 to 16000; with Clef at most 2000), counted the same way for Chinese and English; older messages are dropped first. Default 6000 with Jev: with the skill suggestions' request, which carries every skill's profile (about 22k tokens as Jev counts them), it keeps the state plus the longest question within Jev's 32k. If decisions time out more often, set it lower. Default 2000 with Clef, and a larger value reads as 2000: Clef sometimes reads only about the first 2,100 tokens of what it is sent, and the newest messages come last, so they would be the ones lost.

thetaMax.title: Threshold for max effort
thetaMax.description: The main agent goes to max only when the decision model gives max at least this probability (0 to 1); otherwise it gets the most likely of the other levels. Default 0.5 with either decision model (not calibrated for Clef: Jev's value).

rejudgeEvery.title: Re-decide effort every N steps
rejudgeEvery.description: While a turn runs, the main agent's effort is decided again at every Nth step (0 to 50; 0 turns this off). Dispatching an agent, starting a Workflow or loading a skill also re-decides it.

thetaUp.title: Threshold to raise effort mid-turn
thetaUp.description: A re-decision raises the effort only when the decision model's confidence is at least this (0 to 1). Default 0.4 with either decision model (not calibrated for Clef, whose confidence runs much lower than Jev's: Jev's value).

thetaDown.title: Threshold to lower effort mid-turn
thetaDown.description: A re-decision lowers the effort, by one level at most, only when the decision model's confidence is at least this (0 to 1; never below the raise threshold). Default 0.6 with either decision model (not calibrated for Clef: Jev's value).

holdSteps.title: Steps before effort may drop after a raise
holdSteps.description: After a re-decision raises the effort, it does not lower it again for this many steps (0 to 50).

rejudgeSteps.title: Recent steps read when re-deciding
rejudgeSteps.description: How many of the turn's latest steps the decision model reads when it re-decides (1 to 16): the main agent's last text and the tools it called with how each ended, never file contents or tool output, secrets masked. The context budget bounds them too. Default 16 with Jev (the context budget, not this count, ends what is sent), 4 with Clef.

rejudgeWaitMs.title: Wait for a late re-decision (ms)
rejudgeWaitMs.description: A re-decision is asked while a tool runs; if it is not back when the next request goes out, that request waits this long for it (0 to 2000), then keeps the effort it had and the status line says so.

escalateAfter.title: Failed tool calls before escalating
escalateAfter.description: The main agent, or an agent it dispatched, whose tool calls have failed this many times is asked about again and raised to a higher effort (1 to 20), unless the failures are what the work expects (a test written to fail first, a search that finds nothing). A call you refused yourself never counts; one of your own hooks blocked counts only after /dp hook-block-failures on.

escalateMode.title: How escalating raises the effort
escalateMode.description: one-level: one level up, never past xhigh (the decision model's own pick may go higher when it is sure). max: straight to max. A haiku agent has no effort to raise: it is switched to the model below instead.

escalateLimit.title: Escalations per turn
escalateLimit.description: How many times one turn of the main agent (or one dispatched agent) may be raised for failing tool calls (0 to 10). The failures count from zero again after each escalation.

thetaExpected.title: Threshold to find failures expected
thetaExpected.description: When the decision model rates the failures at least this likely to be what the work expects (0 to 1), nothing is forced: the failures start counting from zero and the effort is left to the ordinary mid-turn rules. Low on purpose: measured on a few hand-written cases, Jev rates failures that are expected 0.15 to 0.72 and ones that are not 0.09 to 0.16 (Clef 0.27 to 0.90 and 0.03 to 0.11). Default 0.25 with either decision model (not calibrated for Clef: Jev's value).

escalateHaikuTo.title: Model a failing haiku agent switches to
escalateHaikuTo.description: A haiku agent has no effort to raise, so when its tool calls keep failing it goes on as this model for the rest of its run: sonnet, opus or fable, or a full model id. An alias is turned into the full id a step needs (the engine takes no alias for a step); a model you named for the agent's work, or ruled out, holds over it. Empty: never switch.

agentFable.title: Let dispatched agents run on fable
agentFable.description: Adds fable to the models the decision model may choose for an agent the main agent dispatches (haiku, sonnet and opus otherwise). Fable costs more than opus. A model you name yourself in your message is used either way.

agentOverride.title: Confidence to override the main agent's model pick
agentOverride.description: When the main agent names a model for an agent it dispatches, the decision model's pick replaces it only at this confidence or above (0 to 1). A model you name yourself in your message is never replaced. Default 0.6 with either decision model (not calibrated for Clef: Jev's value).

skillsMax.title: Skills suggested at most
skillsMax.description: How many skills one message gets suggested at most (0 to 10); fewer, or none, when fewer reach the relevance below.

skillsMinRelevance.title: Least relevance to suggest
skillsMinRelevance.description: The relevance a skill needs to be suggested (0 to 1): how likely the decision model judges that the skill does the kind of work the message asks for, each skill judged on its own after its instructions are re-read. Default 0.75 with either decision model (not calibrated for Clef: Jev's value).

skillsShortlist.title: Skills re-read in the second stage
skillsShortlist.description: How many of the skills the main agent can load, rated highest for a message, are re-read with the opening of their instructions and judged one by one (1 to 10); at most 2 of the skills only you can start are re-read beside them. A skill is re-read only when the first request rated it at least 0.1, and both requests together wait at most the decision timeout.

skillsProfileModel.title: Model that writes skill profiles
skillsProfileModel.description: The model (an alias such as haiku, or a full model id) that writes each skill a short profile in English and Chinese from its SKILL.md, once per version of the file, so the decision model can match a request in either language. It runs in the background through your Claude Code login and uses your plan's usage. A new model writes every profile again.

skillsProfilesPerSession.title: Skill profiles written per session
skillsProfilesPerSession.description: How many missing skill profiles are written at most each time a session starts (0 to 500; 0 writes none). The rest wait for later sessions, so a first run with many skills spreads its cost.

skillsAlwaysListed.title: Skills always listed
skillsAlwaysListed.description: Skills the main agent keeps seeing in its skill listing, by the name the listing gives them (a synced skill with its prefix, such as anthropic-skills:pdf). Every other skill is left out of the listing and suggested only when a message needs it.

skillsNeverSuggested.title: Skills never suggested
skillsNeverSuggested.description: Skills never suggested to the main agent nor pointed out to you, by the name the listing gives them. They stay installed: the Skill tool still loads one by name. find_skill never returns them either.

findSkillMax.title: Skills find_skill returns at most
findSkillMax.description: How many skills the main agent's find_skill tool returns for one query at most (1 to 10); fewer, or none, when fewer reach the relevance below.

findSkillMinRelevance.title: Least relevance find_skill returns
findSkillMinRelevance.description: The relevance a skill needs for find_skill to return it (0 to 1): how likely the decision model judges that the skill does the kind of work the main agent names, each skill judged on its own after its instructions are re-read. Default 0.5 with either decision model (not calibrated for Clef: Jev's value).

workflowMode.title: How Workflow agents are routed
workflowMode.description: rewrite: when the main agent submits a Workflow, the model and effort decided for each agent() call are written into the script before it runs, and the main agent is told what was written. return: the first submission of a Workflow is refused with the recommendation for each agent() call, for the main agent to write in itself; the same Workflow submitted again runs as written.
